sections.html:
Owners can enroll if they file Form DR534 before May 1 of the year they join and the prior year's bill topped $100. Once enrolled, there is no yearly reapplying, with one catch: miss the first installment and the account drops out, and the owner must reapply by April 30 of a later year. Four payments follow a fixed pattern, and the first two are based on last year's gross tax.

Marion County installment schedule
PaymentDueAmountDiscount
FirstJune 30One quarter of last year's gross tax6%
SecondSeptember 30One quarter of last year's gross tax4.5%
ThirdDecember 31One quarter of this year's adjusted tax3%
FourthMarch 31One quarter of this year's adjusted taxNone

A first payment can still be made by July 31, though without the discount. After July 31 the account returns to ordinary annual billing.

The alternative is one lump sum. Paying in November earns 4%, and the discount falls a point a month to 1% in February. Quarterly payers collect bigger percentages on early installments but spread payment over the whole year, so the plan suits owners who prefer steady cash flow to one large bill. If you plan to list soon, remember that the discounted amounts follow last year's bill, which can differ from what the new roll produces.

sections.h2: What happens to the plan when the house sells?
sections.html:
The plan belongs to the tax year, not the seller. If the property changes hands after one or more quarterly payments, the new owner must stay on the plan for that year.

A half-paid plan therefore travels with the house. The buyer takes on the remaining quarters, and your title company needs to know which ones were paid. Ask the collector for a payment history and give copies to both sides.

  • Put the plan details in the disclosure packet so nobody discovers them at the closing table.
  • Check that the settlement statement credits installments you already covered.
  • A buyer who prefers one annual bill should ask the collector whether the account can revert.

The Tax Collector keeps offices around the county, open Monday to Friday from eight to four. Tax deed and certificate questions go only to the main branch, which matters if your parcel carries an old balance.

  • Main office, McPherson Complex, 503 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala.
  • Dunnellon, inside the Rainbow Springs Government Complex.
  • Belleview, in the Belleview Regional Shopping Center on U.S. 441.
  • Forest, at Forest Center on State Road 40 in Silver Springs.
  • State Road 200, at Jasmine Square in Ocala.
  • North, at Ocala Springs Shopping Center on U.S. 441.
  • Summerfield, at Spruce Creek Terrace Shops.
  • Ocala Annex, which serves driver license customers only.

Midweek visits between 9:30 and 10:30 in the morning are the quietest; Mondays, Fridays and month-end days run busiest. The shared number is (352) 368-8200.

sections.h2: Which Marion offices handle value, billing and records?
sections.html:
Three offices touch a sale, and each owns a different question. All are in Ocala but keep separate websites and search tools.

The Property Appraiser at 501 SE 25th Avenue sets value and processes exemptions, taking walk-ins or booked appointments. The Tax Collector issues and collects the bill. The Clerk of Court and Comptroller records deeds, hosts the Value Adjustment Board filings and conducts deed sales.

The statewide calendar sits over all three: January 1 fixes ownership and condition, March 1 closes exemption filings, April 1 is the tangible personal property deadline, and the proposed-tax notice lands in August. The collector's payment page gives November 1 as the due date.

sections.h2: Tourist Development Tax on vacation rentals
sections.html:
Rentals of six months or less owe a 4% Tourist Development Tax, collected from the guest and passed to the Tax Collector. Marion County has no contract with platforms such as Airbnb or VRBO, so the owner has to register, collect and remit directly.

State sales tax in Marion County is 7.5%, made up of 6% plus a 1.5% infrastructure surtax. The tourist tax applies to rent and to fees tied to the stay, such as cleaning and pet fees.

  • The return is due on the first of the following month and is late after the 20th.
  • Operators file every month, collections or not.
  • Late filing costs 10% of the tax for each month, with a $50 floor and a ceiling of half the tax due.
  • An owner who sells or closes the business should notify the office in writing.

Past guest stays leave a paper trail. Gather your registration number, monthly returns and proof of payment, because a careful buyer will want to see the account is current.

The site offers a tax estimator, a request form for a mortgage estimate letter, a change-of-address form and a homestead e-file page, along with a damage report page and a confidential channel for tips about suspected homestead fraud.

Run the estimator at a realistic sale price. A sale resets assessed value, so the buyer's first bill can differ sharply from yours, and lenders ask about that gap. Homestead takes up to $50,000 off the taxable base, with only the first $25,000 applying to school taxes, and the state cap that protects your own assessment ends at transfer.

After you move, file the address change. Notices follow the address on record, and a bill that never arrives still has to be paid.

sections.h2: What happens when Marion County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
April 1 is when routine billing turns into collection. Delinquent parcels are advertised and certificates are sold by June 1. A certificate buyer covers the bill and earns interest but cannot demand money from the owner for two years.

The collector's menu offers an online tax deed application, online purchase of county-held certificates and a delinquent tax page. Homestead parcels start higher at a deed sale. Paying off a certificate sooner costs less, because interest keeps building.

sections.h2: Selling a Marion County house with taxes owed
sections.html:
You can. Back taxes are common in estate sales and in houses left empty, and buyers expect them. Get the exact balance from the collector, and the closing agent deducts it from what the buyer brings.

The state charges seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price in deed stamps, paid at the clerk's recording desk. With an inherited house or several unpaid years, secure a written payoff before you accept an offer. The Clerk's Property Alert Service sends a message whenever a document is recorded under your parcel or name, which helps spot deed fraud.

  1. Request the balance in writing from the collector.
  2. Ask whether any certificate exists on the parcel.
  3. Give the payoff letter to the title company.

Keep the payoff letter and the closing receipt together in your sale file. If the figure changes before closing, ask the collector for a fresh one and pass it along right away.

faqs.q: Who sends the Marion County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Marion County Tax Collector. The Property Appraiser sets the value but does not mail a bill, and the Clerk records deeds and handles deed sales.

faqs.q: What is the first Marion installment due date?
faqs.a: June 30, with a 6% discount on one quarter of last year's gross tax. A late first payment is allowed through July 31 without the discount.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my Marion installment plan?
faqs.a: Yes, for that tax year. If the property sells after payments have started, the new owner continues on the plan.

faqs.q: Do Marion vacation rentals pay a tax beyond sales tax?
faqs.a: Yes, a 4% Tourist Development Tax on rentals of six months or less. The owner pays it to the Tax Collector because no platform contract exists.

faqs.q: Where can I ask about a tax certificate in Marion County?
faqs.a: At the main Tax Collector office, 503 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala. Only the main branch handles tax deed and certificate information.
